headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading error: Airflow can egress broadly while the course agent reads/writes files, handles secrets, and runs shell commands.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A has broad network egress and is an automation orchestrator; B reads/writes files and processes notebook/API inputs. No shared channel is documented, but if B’s outputs are copied into Airflow tasks or files, injected instructions could be executed. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF B’s generated text is copied into Airflow DAGs, task params, or files without sanitization
IF either agent treats file contents as instructions rather than data
mitigations: Use a strict prompt/content delimiter for any B output before Airflow ingestion
Review copied text for instruction-like tokens before execution
Store B outputs in a read-only staging folder
Disable automatic task generation from free text
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between B outputs and Airflow inputs

B_data_leakage.rationale: B explicitly handles configuration secrets and can read/write the filesystem; A has broad network egress. Even though A’s touched data classes are empty, the pair creates a plausible exfiltration path if secrets or papers land in shared files or logs. Uncertainty about shared state does not reduce the risk enough, so the higher severity is chosen.
conditions: IF secrets or sensitive papers are present in files accessible to B
IF A can reach external endpoints while receiving those files or logs
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories
Rotate any exposed API keys before pairing
Restrict A’s egress to approved destinations only
Run B in a separate workspace with no secret-bearing files
requires-engineering: add per-file access controls and secret scanning

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A is an orchestrator with broad egress, while B can execute shell commands, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and write the filesystem. They do not both show unrestricted write to the same directory, but overlapping mutable operations create conflict risk if they share a workspace or runtime. Lack of stated locking escalates uncertainty.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same writable workspace
IF Airflow tasks and B subprocesses modify overlapping files without locks
mitigations: Assign separate working directories
Avoid concurrent writes to shared artifacts
Serialize task execution around mutable files
Check for lock files before writes
requires-engineering: add workspace-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: A’s automation role and B’s agentic RAG workflow make it plausible that B consumes A-produced outputs as inputs. If B treats those outputs as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream shell, package, or API actions. No verification step is documented, so the safer higher severity applies.
conditions: IF B ingests A-generated text, plans, or metadata without verification
IF B then triggers shell commands or API calls based on that input
mitigations: Require human review before B acts on A outputs
Add schema validation for A-to-B handoffs
Log and diff A outputs before execution
Disable autonomous action on low-confidence results
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between agents

E_compliance.rationale: B explicitly handles configuration secrets and academic data, while A is an Airflow orchestrator with broad egress. The profiles do not show a residency mismatch or regulated data class like PHI, but differing handling of secrets and retention-sensitive artifacts can still create policy mismatch if shared. A is cited for egress; B for the sensitive classes.
conditions: IF regulated or confidential course data is processed through both agents
IF retention or logging policies differ between Airflow and the course stack
mitigations: Document which data classes may flow through each agent
Disable verbose logging for secrets
Set explicit retention limits on shared artifacts
Review data residency for any external API calls
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
